mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays flat or slightly above, weekday discretionary trips remain suppressed and RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline for the full period.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in PARKS mobility below zero signals reduced outdoor leisure and companion shopping activity, which lowers retail-and-recreation visits within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 after being positive the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the two weeks after PARKS crosses from positive to negative.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES remains depressed, households consolidate errands into essential trips and postpone discretionary shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above baseline and WORKPLACES stays below baseline throughout the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in TRANSIT toward baseline acts as a reopening signal and feeds through to more discretionary retail visits within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a sub-baseline level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within one week after TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain of at least 3 points from below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upswing in PARKS combined with flatter RESIDENTIAL activity marks warm-weather leisure substitution into nearby retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains positive for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks despite PARKS staying positive for two weeks and RESIDENTIAL not falling.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay weak, people substitute toward at-home routines and away from discretionary errands, which keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL is above baseline and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous lift in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT above their recent levels indicates easing mobility frictions; that combined easing should increase retail visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week from sub-baseline levels
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase together from below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES cuts access to shopping districts and suppresses discretionary visits, so RETAIL_REC falls within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below baseline in a tightening-restrictions period.
